questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The weather patterns ______ that we will have a winter season, perhaps a good one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"suggest"**.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given options, **"suggest"** is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
 
• The verb changes only in third person singular (he, she, it, a person, a thing), where it gets the suffix -s or -es.
 
• The given sentence has the plural subject i.e. patterns, so 'suggest' will be the acceptable answer.
 
• Thus, option 3) is the correct alternative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let us see the use of 's' or 'es' in simple present tense.

 
• For the third person singular (she, he, it*), we add -s to the base form of verb.

 
 
• **Example: **He **prepares** breakfast daily.
 
 
 
• We add -es to verbs that end in -ch, -ss, -sh, -x, or -zz.
 
 
• **Example: **Buzz - Buzzes, watch - watches, Dish - Dishes, Ex - Exes, Dress - Dresses.
 
 
 
• When a verb ends in a consonant and -y, then y is changed to the I and the suffix- es is added.
 
 
• **Example: **study - studies.
 
 
 
• However, we simply add -s when the verb ends in a vowel and -y.
 
 
• **Example:** pay - pays; enjoy- enjoys

• **Hereby:** When expressing yourself in an official or formal manner, you use the phrase "hereby."

 
 
• **Example: **I **hereby** authorize you to execute any and all contracts on my behalf.
 
 
 
• ***Yet:*** It is an adverb that we employ to describe a period of time that begins in the past and ends in the present.
 
 
• It is often used in present perfect negative assertions or queries. Usually, it is in the final position.
 
• **Example:** Her advice seems strange, **yet** I believe she's right.
 
 
 
• **Though: **It** **is used to show contrast or modification between information in a clause and that provided in a prior sentence or sentences.
 
 
• **Example: **My house was not empty **though** I was gone.

• In the given options, **"must**" is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
 
• "**Must**" is a verb that denotes obligation, commands, and recommendations. It can only be referred to in the present and future.

• Thus, ***option 3)*** is the correct alternative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let us understand the usage of other options.

 
• **Have to: **The word **"have to"** is frequently used to indicate that something is required.

 
 
• **Example: **Children **have to** come to school in proper uniform.
 
 
 
• **Lest: **The preposition lest denotes either for fear of, or to avoid. The speaker then adds something they believe should be avoided.
 
 
• **Example: **He gripped his brother's arm **lest** he be trampled by the mob.
 
 
 
• **Would: **The past tense of the verb will is "would." It is used to talk about the past because it is a past tense. to discuss hypotheses (when we imagine something).
 
• **Example: **I** would** go to the store tomorrow, if I didn't have school.
